title: stabilize-late-usage-watermarks-and-fix-tiered-proration-bleed
creator: Lena Park
description:
Summary:
We intermittently generate invoices that include duplicated or misplaced rate-limit credit lines when late usage pulses or retry storms arrive after the proration boundary for a billing window. Root cause analysis points to two interacting issues: 1) no deterministic export epoch/watermark per-customer, so late pulses are merged into adjacent windows inconsistently; 2) credits from transient rate-limit events lack an origin tag and are applied by the export reconciler without idempotent sequencing, causing 'proration bleed' across tier boundaries when customers swap plans mid-cycle.

Why it matters:
- Customer invoices show unexpected negative/credit line items or doubled credits, triggering support tickets and manual adjustments.
- Enterprise customers see accounting variance with NetSuite exports (out-of-order seqnums), affecting revenue recognition and requiring manual journal entries.

Proposed fix (high level):
1) Introduce a per-customer export epoch (ledger_watermark_epoch) that advances monotonically and fences which usage pulses belong to a given invoice cycle. Exports will only include usage with pulse_timestamp <= epoch_cutoff (and tag out-of-order pulses for backfill).
2) Add an origin and event_seq tag to all rate-limit credit emissions (origin: rate_limit, retry_suppress, backfill). The reconciler will require a matching (customer, origin, event_seq) idempotency key before generating credit lines.
3) Implement a deterministic ordering step in the export generator: sort by (customer_id, epoch, pulse_timestamp, event_seq) and attach an export_seqnum to every emitted invoice line to make NetSuite/Stripe imports idempotent.
4) Provide a short, configurable holdback window (default 5 minutes) for near-boundary pulses; pulses inside the holdback are buffered and reconciled with the epoch advancement to avoid jitter on edge-case plan swaps. Longer-late pulses are routed to a backfill pipeline that produces correction exports and a soft-credit audit trail.

Technical notes:
- The epoch will be stored in the billing ledger table as ledger_watermark_epoch (bigint) with last_export_seqnum to allow safe resume in leader failover.
- Backfill corrections must produce negative and positive adjustment lines with a reason_code and original_pulse_timestamp. These lines will be exported separately to avoid merging into the canonical invoice payload and to make downstream accounting reconciliation deterministic.
- The reconciler will add small, human-friendly metadata to exported lines (exported_by: reconciler-v2, export_run_id, origin_tag) for auditability.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Holding pulses increases apparent latency for some usage. Mitigation: default holdback is small (5m) and can be lowered per-customer in Dedicated.
- Risk: Backfill volume could spike. Mitigation: throttle backfill runner and add priority ordering to prevent saturating Netsuite/Stripe export quotas.

Acceptance criteria:
- All billing exports include export_seqnum and origin_tag and persist last_export_seqnum in the ledger for leader resume.
- Nightly audit job shows reduction of invoice credit duplicates by >= 95% on a 7-day rolling window for previously impacted customers.
- Correction/backfill exports are generated with clear reason_codes and do not mutate historical canonical invoices (they append adjustment lines only).
- NetSuite/Stripe test import (shadow mode) shows idempotent behavior when reapplying the same export file twice.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for epoch advance logic, idempotency keys, and ordering comparator.
- Integration test: simulated retry storm generator to produce out-of-order pulses and verify reconciler produces deterministic export lines.
- Staging run with shadow-exports to NetSuite/Stripe for a representative subset of customers for two billing cycles.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge reconciler changes behind a feature flag (billing.reconciler.v2).
2) Deploy read-only epoch persistence to collect metrics and run audits for 48 hours.
3) Enable holdback logic for <1% of customers and monitor latency/credit duplication metrics.
4) Gradually increase to 100% and enable backfill runner.
5) After two billing cycles of stable metrics, flip feature flag off for rollback path and then remove old reconciler code.
acceptance_criteria: export lines include export_seqnum, origin_tag, export_run_id
ledger_watermark_epoch persists and prevents cross-window pulse merging
invoice credit duplicates reduced by >=95% for impacted customers on a 7-day rolling window
correction exports are append-only and have explicit reason_code and original_pulse_timestamp
NetSuite/Stripe shadow import is idempotent when reprocessing same export file
plan: Schema migration: add ledger_watermark_epoch and last_export_seqnum (deferred indexes applied offline)
Implement origin/event_seq tagging at rate-limit credit emission points (token-bucket and retry suppress paths)
Reconciler: deterministic sorter, export_seqnum assignment, and idempotency check against (customer, origin, event_seq)
Holdback buffer implementation with per-customer ttl and metric instrumentation
Backfill runner to produce corrections with throttling and priority queues
Shadow exports to Stripe/NetSuite for two cycles; validate imports and run reconciliation audits
Feature flag rollout and gradual ramp-up with monitoring dashboards

2026-03-12 PM feedback (Rajesh Nair): prefer customer-configurable holdback per Dedicated accounts; added as follow-up task in project plan.
